steps.title: The ply's strain in its fibre axes
steps.source: Finite element theory, 6. Ply stresses in material axes
steps.text: The solve's strain at ply 1 (45°), element 29, bottom face, turned into the ply's fibre axes. The probe table shows the same three values.

steps.title: The ply's stress from its strain
steps.text: The ply's stiffness in its fibre axes, from its elastic constants, times the strain.

steps.title: The maximum stress criterion
steps.text: Each stress against its own strength; the smallest ratio governs: tension across the fibres (sigma_2 reaching F2t, a matrix-dominated mode). The failure index the results show is 1/R.

steps.title: The loading at first-ply failure
steps.text: The model is linear, so every stress grows with the loading: the first ply fails at the factor times what is applied.

steps.title: The Tsai-Hill criterion
steps.text: The three stresses in one expression, with the tensile or compressive strength by the sign of each stress. The laminate fails when the sum reaches one.

given.what: tensile strength along the fibres, F1t
tensile strength across the fibres, F2t

steps.note: FI here is the Tsai-Hill sum. The failure index the results show is 1/R, the square root of this sum: both reach one at the same loading.
